sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: This succession plan outlines leadership continuity measures for the company’s eight mission-critical roles over the next twelve months. The review evaluates internal bench strength, identifies high-potential successors, and clarifies readiness timelines (Ready Now, Ready in 6–12 Months, Ready in 12–24 Months). Two roles currently present elevated risk due to limited internal depth, requiring accelerated development and external mapping. Immediate emergency coverage assignments have been confirmed with each division head.

sections.heading: Critical Roles and Readiness Status
sections.body: The Chief Revenue Officer role has one Ready Now successor (Marissa Holt, SVP Enterprise Sales) and one Ready in 12–24 Months candidate (Dev Patel, VP Channel Strategy). The VP Manufacturing position has no Ready Now successor; Carlos Jiménez (Plant Director, Monterrey) is assessed as Ready in 6–12 Months pending financial acumen development. The Chief Information Security Officer role is supported by a strong bench, with Priya Nandakumar (Director, Cyber Defense) designated Ready Now and actively participating in board risk briefings. The Head of Regulatory Affairs remains a single-incumbent risk with only interim coverage identified.

sections.heading: High-Potential Talent Identification
sections.body: Nine individuals were confirmed as enterprise high-potential (HiPo) candidates through the November 2025 talent calibration process. Among them, Lena Brooks (GM, Northeast Region) and Ahmed El-Sayed (Director, Supply Chain Optimization) demonstrate cross-functional leadership capability and consistent top-quartile performance ratings. Both have completed strategic leadership assessments indicating readiness acceleration potential. Diversity metrics were reviewed to ensure equitable representation in succession slates, with 56% of identified successors representing underrepresented groups.

sections.heading: Development Plans and Acceleration Actions
sections.body: Targeted development actions include executive mentoring, P&L exposure, and board presentation opportunities. For Carlos Jiménez, a six-month rotational assignment within Corporate Finance will address identified capability gaps tied to capital planning and cost governance. Marissa Holt will participate in investor relations roadshows to broaden market-facing leadership exposure. All Ready in 6–12 Months candidates have documented development milestones with quarterly progress reviews facilitated by HR Business Partners.

sections.heading: Emergency Succession and Risk Mitigation
sections.body: Emergency successors have been designated for each critical role to ensure operational continuity in the event of sudden vacancy. For the VP Manufacturing role, interim oversight would transfer to COO Thomas Reinhardt for up to 90 days while an internal or external search is conducted. The Head of Regulatory Affairs gap requires immediate external pipeline development; an executive search firm has been engaged to map qualified candidates by Q2 2026. Monthly risk reviews will monitor attrition indicators and retention actions for all primary successors.

text_content: **Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Roles (FY2026)**

As of 2026-05-01, 6 roles are designated as critical: CEO, CFO, COO, Chief Information Officer, Chief Revenue Officer, and General Counsel. This enterprise-level designation reflects board and executive leadership inputs and aligns with FY2026 strategic priorities. The inventory establishes a common scope for succession assessment, governance, and resource allocation across key functions.

Bench analysis indicates bench coverage is 4 of 6 critical roles with at least one Ready-Now successor (67%). The Ready-Now slates populate CEO, CFO, COO, and Chief Revenue Officer, providing immediate continuity. Succession strength is quantified by readiness level, depth (number of successors per role) and performance; gaps among non-Ready candidates are tracked in the high-potential development pipeline.

Two critical roles have no Ready-Now successor: Chief Information Officer and General Counsel. These emergency succession gaps are material to enterprise operational risk and are prioritized for immediate review. Detailed remediation actions, successor development trajectories, and emergency coverage protocols are documented in the "High-Potential Successor Slate, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps" section; risk owners will report monthly directly to the succession governance committee and stakeholders.
